questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: A mix between academic opportunities, including improving my English, curiosity of how studying at a different university would be and exploring a different city.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the university provided courses that I was interested in and that the university seemed structured. Also, the city and student environment.

questions.answer: It was relatively easy. University of Amsterdam made it easy for exchange students to find the essential information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't as such.

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy but a bit stressful.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it is essential to beware of deadlines and check your email constantly. Otherwise you might miss the opportunity to get housing offered.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy once you understood the proces but I didn't recieve enough information.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to register for courses through a page you log in to with your student-id and password. It was essential to register for courses on the exact dates and time that the registration opened up.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Through the university page.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I almost didn't get one of my courses because I was not aware that I had to register at 8 am exactly to be secured a spot since the registration process is much different at the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To register at the exact time that registration opens.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some courses were at a higher level than others but most were quite compatible to the university of copenhagen in difficulty.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Lectures were similar but classes were different in that they were often taught by the lectures themselves instead of a TA.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Labour Economics, Philisophy of Science, Development Economics, Game Theory and Natural Resource Economics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would highly reccomend Philosophy of Science and Labour Economics. Philosophy of Science was a difficult but very interesting course with a highly compentent lecturer who was very enganged in the learning process of his students. There was very little emphasis on the exam during the course which really opened op my curiosity for all the different texts that we read. Labour Economics was a good course since we were introduced to so many research papers which inspired many ideas in terms of what kind of things you could research or methods to apply in a bachelor or master thesis. I would also reccomend Game Theory even though I was not too satisfied with the tutorial classes since the lectures were good and the material very interesting.

questions.answer: There was a student council, sport activities, different bars and cafés on campus.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I don't know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I mostly stayed in Amsterdam because there are so many great things to experience there. Otherwise, Den Haag, Haarlem, Rotterdam, tulip fields

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy since the locals speak a great English.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Joining a study group for a course where there is a mix of local students and exchange students. Join smaller classes where it is easier to chat to people in the breaks.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I would not say that the cultural differences were challenging per say.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The multiculturalism.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Beware of how the housing process and registration process works, get a bike, and interact with students in your class

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Exploring a different city and culture and getting to know new people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The workload the first two months and being in a place where you do not know many people at first.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.answer: Yes
